name: Gym for confidence (gymmaxxing)

card.summary: Resistance and general exercise as a route to self-confidence and body satisfaction; exercise has some mood evidence, confidence claims are thinly tested.
card.note: Evidence on exercise concerns mood and depression more than confidence or looks.

quick.overview:
Gymmaxxing refers to training in the gym to improve physique and, proponents say, confidence. It is listed as a training-related lifestyle practice.

Wikipedia reports exercise has short and long-term mood effects and may affect self-esteem, though that claim is described tentatively.
quick.mechanism: Proponents point to physique change and a sense of mastery. Researchers describe exercise effects on mood, including raised positive affect.[1]
quick.risks: Injury risk exists with any training. Wikipedia describes evidence quality on well-being outcomes as mixed.[1]

lead: Gymmaxxing is a looksmaxxing term for gym training pursued to improve physique and, as proponents describe it, confidence.

Wikipedia states that consistent aerobic exercise may affect self-esteem and overall well-being, but gives no effect sizes, and reports the strongest evidence for depression, where a 2024 network meta-analysis of 218 trials found exercise comparable to psychotherapy and medication with limited confidence.[1]
No study found specifically examines gym training as a confidence strategy in looksmaxxing.

paras: Wikipedia describes exercise-induced mood effects as partly transient and the evidence as mixed, mostly moderate to low quality.[1]
No studies found on gymmaxxing for confidence specifically. Broader exercise and mental-health research is summarised on Wikipedia.[1]
